prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: Across all five frames, the camera wearer is roughly 0.5–1.0 m from the foreground table and its objects, while the windows are about 1–2 m ahead and the vegetation beyond them is several metres away. The table occupies the lower foreground, with cups, bottles, a paper-towel roll, a dark appliance or container, and food items standing above it; nearer objects appear brighter and partly occlude the tabletop and one another. The viewpoint shifts mainly rightward and slightly turns across the sequence, bringing the right-hand tabletop objects closer to the image centre while the window frames and outdoor background slide left; there is no clear person approaching or retreating. The map makes front-to-back ordering and object separation clearer than RGB, but it is unreliable around thin window bars, reflective glass, object boundaries, and the bright lower edge, and its grayscale does not support precise metric distances.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates several tabletop objects—mainly cups, bottles, potted plants, a vase-like object, and a bowl—against an otherwise unlabeled scene, showing their left-to-right arrangement and which silhouettes overlap. Detected objects are roughly within 0.5–1.5 m of the camera wearer and close together, generally separated by only a few centimetres to a few tens of centimetres; no person is consistently segmented. Across the five frames, detections enter, leave, or move laterally in the image as the camera turns right, with the later frames emphasizing objects on the right side of the table. Compared with RGB, the map clarifies individual instance boundaries where dark or similarly coloured objects overlap, but it omits most of the table, windows, and background and appears unreliable in labels and consistency—for example, a likely snack package is labeled “car,” some objects change class or disappear, and masks only cover parts of visible objects.
descriptions.pose: The pose map contains only one small yellow body-like detection near the lower-left area of the first frame and no stable body or hand skeletons in the remaining four frames. The RGB strip shows no clearly visible person, so facing direction, gaze toward the camera wearer, inter-person distance, and anyone else’s arm reach cannot be determined; the isolated detection is spatially inconsistent with a recognizable body and is likely unreliable. No approach, retreat, or turning by a person can be tracked across the sequence because the detection vanishes immediately and does not recur. Unlike RGB, a reliable pose map could expose articulated body or hand locations, but here it adds no dependable spatial information beyond indicating a probable false or fragmentary detection partly near the frame edge.
